mainTopic: רבי שמעון and רבי אליעזר on the offerings of the כהן משיח and the נשיא for טומאת מקדש, and the start of the new פרק on leaders who leave office
overview: The גמרא first settles a contradiction in רבי שמעון's view of the כהן משיח. One statement is about a poor person's offering (דלות), and the other is about a very poor person's offering (דלי דלות). חזקיה then finds a source for why the כהן גדול is not liable for טומאת מקדש: the words 'מתוך הקהל'. After challenges from the נשיא and from regular כהנים, רבא rereads that פסוק to mean someone whose sin-offering matches an ordinary person's. רבי יוחנן limits רבי אליעזר's ruling that the נשיא brings a goat to טומאת מקדש alone, and רב פפא proves this from the fact that רבי אליעזר never mentions the משיח's bull. רבי יוחנן adds that רבי אליעזר agrees the נשיא brings no אשם, so a ברייתא requiring an אשם תלוי remains a difficulty. The פרק then ends, and a new משנה asks what a כהן משיח or a נשיא brings after leaving office. The גמרא begins questioning that משנה's wording, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The two statements contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that two statements about רבי שמעון's view of the כהן משיח clash.
steps.simpleTranslation: These two statements are difficult, because they contradict one another!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that two teachings about רבי שמעון's view do not fit together. This sets up the next step, where an answer will be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One teaching has רבי שמעון holding that the כהן משיח is liable for the sliding-scale offering, except in the case of טומאת מקדש. The other has him exempting the כהן משיח. Both cannot be true as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: They are difficult; they raise a problem
With each other; one against the other
The anointed כהן גדול

phrases.english: They are difficult, one against the other!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by raising a contradiction between two earlier statements.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two statements about רבי שמעון's view of the כהן משיח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One statement makes the כהן משיח liable and the other exempts him, so they contradict.

steps.title: One statement is about a poor person's offering, the other about a very poor person's
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the statements deal with two different levels of the sliding-scale offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: It is not difficult. Here it is talking about poverty, and there it is talking about extreme poverty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the contradiction. He says each statement is talking about a different level of poverty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן עולה ויורד changes with a person's wealth: a poor person (דלות) brings birds, and a very poor person (דלי דלות) brings a flour offering. The statement that makes the כהן משיח liable is about the poor level. The statement that exempts him is about the very poor level, so there is no clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no problem
Poverty: the level where one brings birds
Extreme poverty: the level where one brings a flour offering
The sliding-scale offering, which goes up or down with a person's wealth

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two levels. דלות means poor and brings birds. דלי דלות means extremely poor and brings flour.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
It is not difficult. Here, it is about poverty,
there, it is about extreme poverty.
phrases.notes: Literally 'the poorest of the poor': someone so poor he can only bring a flour offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא. כָּאן – בְּדַלּוּת, כָּאן – בְּדַלֵּי דַלּוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each statement refers to a different level of poverty
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both statements seemed to describe the same situation, so they appeared to clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: Liability applies at the level of דלות, and the exemption applies at the level of דלי דלות.

steps.title: רבי שמעון agrees with רבי עקיבא on one point and disagrees on the other
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא spells out where רבי שמעון stands compared to רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון holds like רבי עקיבא in one thing and disagrees with him in one thing. He holds like רבי עקיבא that at the level of extreme poverty the כהן משיח is exempt, and he disagrees with him about the level of poverty.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא finishes his answer by showing how רבי שמעון's view lines up with רבי עקיבא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא exempts the כהן משיח at both levels. רבי שמעון agrees about the very poor level (the flour offering), but at the poor level he holds the כהן משיח is liable. This explains why רבי שמעון seems to say both 'liable' and 'exempt.'

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like the opinion of
In one matter
He disagrees with him
Exempt

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון holds that the כהן משיח is exempt at the level of דלי דלות, like רבי עקיבא, but liable at the level of דלות, unlike רבי עקיבא.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בַּחֲדָא
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon holds like Rabbi Akiva in one matter
and disagrees with him in one matter:

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּדַלֵּי דַלּוּת דְּפָטוּר,
phrases.english: he holds like Rabbi Akiva about extreme poverty, that he is exempt,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן משיח, who is exempt from the flour offering.

phrases.english: and he disagrees with him about poverty.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בַּחֲדָא וּפְלִיג עֲלֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב הונא's answer and spells out what it means for רבי שמעון's position.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי שמעון holds the כהן משיח is exempt at the level of דלי דלות, like רבי עקיבא, and liable at the level of דלות, against רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Why does רבי שמעון exempt the כהן גדול?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and חזקיה asks what source רבי שמעון relies on.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'except that the כהן גדול is not liable, etc.' חזקיה said: What is the reason of רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה's statement that the כהן גדול is not liable for טומאת מקדש. חזקיה asks for the source, which sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון says the כהן גדול is not liable for entering the מקדש or eating קדשים while impure. The גמרא wants to know why he is treated differently from everyone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.: the quote from the משנה continues
What is the reason?
Entering the מקדש or eating its holy food while impure

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל חַיָּיב כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Except that the High Priest is not liable, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. It means he is not liable for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן?
phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said: What is the reason of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה and a new question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for רבי שמעון's ruling that a כהן גדול is not liable for טומאת מקדש.

steps.title: The source: 'from the midst of the congregation'
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה learns from the פסוק that the law applies only to someone whose offering matches the community's.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'That soul shall be cut off from the midst of the congregation.' This means someone whose offering is the same as the congregation's. That leaves out this one, the כהן גדול, whose offering is not the same as the congregation's.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers his own question with a פסוק about someone who becomes impure and enters the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מתוך הקהל' are read to mean that the law covers someone who is like the community in his offerings. The כהן גדול brings his own different offering, so he is left out of this law.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall be cut off (the punishment of כרת)
The congregation; the community of ישראל
Equal; the same as
Is excluded; is left out

phrases.english: As it is written: “That soul shall be cut off from the midst of the congregation,”
one whose offering is equal to the congregation's.

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא זֶה שֶׁאֵין קׇרְבָּנוֹ שָׁוֶה לַקָּהָל.
phrases.english: This one is excluded, as his offering is not equal to the congregation's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'מתוך הקהל' limits the law to someone whose offering matches the community's, and that leaves out the כהן גדול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, 'קרבנו שוה לקהל', is the test that the next steps challenge. In step 11, רבא ends up rereading the פסוק in a different way.

steps.title: Then the נשיא should be exempt too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the נשיא also brings a different offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the נשיא too: his offering is not the same as the congregation's!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges חזקיה's rule. The נשיא also brings his own special offering, so by this rule he should also be exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נשיא brings a goat for his sin, which is different from what a regular person brings. If being different exempts the כהן גדול, it should also exempt the נשיא, even though the משנה does not exempt him.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is the rule
The king or head of the nation
Also; too

phrases.english: If so, the king too –
his offering is not equal to the congregation's!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule derived in step 5.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule seems to exempt the נשיא as well, which goes against the משנה.

steps.title: The נשיא shares the community's יום הכיפורים atonement
steps.stepSummary: The נשיא counts as equal to the community because he gets atonement with them on יום הכיפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is equal to them in the atonement of יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the נשיא is equal to the community where it counts: on יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכיפורים the נשיא is atoned for by the same offerings as everyone else. The כהן גדול brings his own פר instead, so he is truly different, and the rule still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Atonement
יום כיפור, the Day of Atonement

phrases.english: He is equal in the atonement of Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the נשיא in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Refining the definition of 'equal to the community'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any difference in offerings seemed to exclude a person from the law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sharing the יום הכיפורים atonement is enough to count as equal to the community.

steps.title: Then regular כהנים should be exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that regular כהנים do not share the community's יום הכיפורים atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the כהנים too are not equal to the congregation in the atonement of יום הכיפורים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the new definition. Regular כהנים are atoned for differently on יום הכיפורים, so they should be exempt too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכיפורים the כהנים are atoned for through the כהן גדול's פר, not through the community's goat. By the test from step 7, they would not count as equal to the community.

keyTerms.meaning: Regular כהנים (not the כהן גדול)
They are not equal

phrases.english: If so, priests too

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁווּ לַקָּהָל בְּכַפָּרָה דְּיוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים!
phrases.english: are not equal to the congregation in the atonement of Yom Kippur!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the definition given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The definition of 'equal' as sharing the יום הכיפורים atonement
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Regular כהנים do not share that atonement, so they would wrongly be exempt.

steps.title: כהנים are equal to the community in the rest of the year's מצוות
steps.stepSummary: Regular כהנים count as equal because their offerings match the community's for all other מצוות all year.
steps.simpleTranslation: כהנים are equal to the congregation in the rest of the מצוות of the whole year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that regular כהנים are equal to everyone else for the rest of the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being equal can come either from the יום הכיפורים atonement, as with the נשיא, or from the rest of the year's מצוות, as with the כהנים. The answer assumes the כהן גדול is equal in neither, but the next step challenges exactly that.

keyTerms.meaning: The other מצוות
The whole year

phrases.english: Priests are equal to the congregation
in the rest of the מצוות of the entire year.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֲנִים שָׁווּ לַקָּהָל בִּשְׁאָר מִצְוֹת דְּשָׁנָה כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from regular כהנים in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widening the ways one can count as 'equal to the community'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the יום הכיפורים atonement seemed to count as being equal.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sharing the offerings for the rest of the year's מצוות also counts as being equal to the community. The next step shows this proves too much.

steps.title: The anointed priest also matches the community in other מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that by the standard of step 9, the משיח would also count as equal to the community, so the פסוק could not exclude him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the anointed priest is also equal to the community in the rest of the מצוות of the year!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 9. If matching the community in other מצוות is enough, then the משיח matches too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said regular כהנים count as equal because their offerings match the community's in other מצוות all year. The משיח also brings ordinary offerings in other מצוות, so he would count as equal too. But חזקיה's whole point was to exclude the משיח, so this standard breaks his reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The anointed priest, meaning the כהן גדול
The other מצוות of the whole year
Equal, the same as

phrases.english: The anointed priest, too,
is equal regarding the rest of the מצוות of the year!
phrases.notes: He means equal to the community, using the same standard the גמרא just used for regular כהנים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the answer in step 9 proves too much
steps.kashyaTarget: The standard from step 9 that matching the community in other מצוות is enough
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that standard is right, the משיח also passes it, so the פסוק can no longer exclude him

steps.title: רבא rereads the verse: one whose sin-offering matches individuals
steps.stepSummary: רבא drops the earlier approach. He reads the פסוק as referring to someone whose sin-offering matches that of individuals, and says the word קהל means exactly those people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Say it this way. The פסוק means one whose sin-offering is equal to that of individuals. And who is that? The community.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new way to read the פסוק so that it still leaves out the משיח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the test was whether someone's offering matches the community's. רבא changes the test to whether someone's sin-offering matches an ordinary individual's, and says the word קהל refers to those ordinary people. The משיח fails this test. Per רש״י, if he sins by an ordinary mistake that did not come from his own wrong ruling, he brings no sin-offering at all, unlike an ordinary person. So he stays excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: Say it this way, used to offer a new reading
Individuals, ordinary people
Community, the word in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, the פסוק excludes the משיח because his sin-offering rules are unlike an ordinary person's (for a plain mistaken act he brings none at all), and not because of any comparison to the community's offerings.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
Say it this way:
One whose sin-offering is equal to that of individuals,
and who is that? The community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed approach of steps 5 through 9 with a new reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק compares people's offerings to the community's offerings
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק compares people's sin-offering to an individual's, and the משיח's special פר is different

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits רבי אליעזר's ruling to defiling the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's view in the משנה that the נשיא brings a goat. רבי יוחנן says this applies only to טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, because כרת is stated there just as it is for a fixed sin-offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: The king brings a goat, and so on. רבי יוחנן said: רבי אליעזר said this only about defiling the Temple or its holy foods, since כרת is stated there, as it is for a fixed sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה: רבי אליעזר's ruling that the נשיא brings a שעיר. רבי יוחנן explains that this ruling applies to only one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a נשיא brings a goat for sins that carry כרת. Defiling the Temple also carries כרת, so רבי אליעזר treats it like those sins. For hearing a voice and an oath of the lips, which carry no כרת, the נשיא brings the regular sliding-scale offering.

keyTerms.meaning: The king or leader
A male goat, the נשיא's special sin-offering
Entering the Temple or eating holy foods while impure
Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for certain deliberate sins
A fixed sin-offering, which does not change based on wealth

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying the נשיא is exempt in the other cases. In those cases he simply brings the regular sliding-scale offering like everyone else.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
The king brings a goat, etc.
Rabbi Yochanan said:
Rabbi Eliezer said this only
regarding defiling the Temple or its holy foods,
since כרת is stated about it
as with a fixed sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר's goat for the נשיא applies only to טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, because כרת is involved, as with a fixed sin-offering

steps.title: רב פפא proves רבי יוחנן right from the missing anointed priest
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא argues that if רבי אליעזר meant all the cases, he should also have said the משיח brings a פר for hearing a voice and an oath of the lips. Since he did not, his ruling must be about טומאת מקדש, where the משיח is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: That makes sense too. If you think רבי אליעזר meant all the cases, then since the נשיא's goat and the משיח's bull both take the place of an individual's sin-offering, he should also teach that the משיח brings a bull for hearing a voice and an oath of the lips. Since he does not mention the משיח, learn from this that he is talking about defiling the Temple, where the משיח is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a proof for רבי יוחנן's reading from what רבי אליעזר left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נשיא's goat and the משיח's bull are parallel, since each replaces an ordinary person's sin-offering. If רבי אליעזר's ruling covered all the cases, he should have mentioned the משיח's bull alongside the goat. His silence makes sense only in the case of טומאת מקדש, where the משיח brings nothing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: That also makes sense, used to introduce supporting logic
A bull, the משיח's special sin-offering
Hearing a voice, failing to testify after being put under oath
An oath of the lips, a broken spoken oath
Learn from this

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
So too it is reasonable,
for if it would enter your mind
that Rabbi Eliezer is speaking about all of them,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all three cases in the משנה: hearing a voice, an oath of the lips, and defiling the Temple.

phrases.english: since the goat of the king and the bull of the anointed priest
stand in place of an individual's sin-offering,
let him also teach:
the anointed priest brings a bull
for hearing a voice and an oath of the lips.
Rather, since he does not teach about the anointed priest,
learn from this
that he is referring to defiling the Temple or its holy foods,
where the anointed priest is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's statement
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's view that רבי אליעזר spoke only about טומאת מקדש וקדשיו
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר does not mention the משיח's bull, which makes sense only where the משיח is exempt

steps.title: רב הונא son of רב נתן suggests רבי אליעזר follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן suggests that רבי אליעזר may mean all the cases, and leaves out the משיח because he agrees with רבי עקיבא that the משיח is exempt in all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב נתן, said to רב פפא: How do you know? Maybe רבי אליעזר is talking about all the cases, and about the משיח he holds like רבי עקיבא, who says the משיח is exempt in all of them!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא's proof is challenged by offering another reason why רבי אליעזר did not mention the משיח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא assumed the משיח was left out because he is exempt only in the case of טומאת מקדש. רב הונא says he may be left out because, following רבי עקיבא, he is exempt in every case. If so, רבי אליעזר's goat could still apply to all the cases, and the proof falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know?
Perhaps
Exempt in all of them

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Natan said to Rav Pappa:
From where do you know this?
Perhaps Rabbi Eliezer is referring to all of them,
and regarding the anointed priest he holds like Rabbi Akiva,
who says:
the anointed priest is exempt in all of them!
phrases.notes: He means exempt from the sliding-scale offering in all three cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's proof
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב פפא's proof only, not רבי יוחנן's ruling itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The missing mention of the משיח could be explained by רבי עקיבא's view that he is exempt in every case

steps.title: רבי עקיבא never exempts the anointed priest from his bull
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that רבי עקיבא exempts the משיח only from the sliding-scale offering, never from his own bull, so the original proof stands. The discussion ends there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Does רבי עקיבא exempt him from a bull? And there is nothing more to say.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends his proof and ends the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's exemption covers only the sliding-scale offering. He never said the משיח is free from his special פר. So if רבי אליעזר's ruling covered every case, he still should have mentioned the משיח's bull. His silence still points to טומאת מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Does he exempt him?, a question expecting the answer no
And nothing more, meaning the discussion is closed

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's limit stands: according to רבי אליעזר, the נשיא brings a goat only for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, and רב פפא's proof from the missing משיח survives.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רב פפא answering רב הונא.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מִי פָּטַר לֵיהּ מִפַּר?
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Akiva exempt him from a bull?
And nothing more.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מִי פָּטַר לֵיהּ מִפַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב הונא's challenge and keeps רב פפא's proof
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the cited opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא exempts the משיח completely, so leaving him out proves nothing
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא exempts the משיח only from the sliding-scale offering, so the bull should still have been mentioned

steps.title: רבי אליעזר agrees the king brings no guilt-offering
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן adds a limit to רבי אליעזר's view: even though the נשיא brings a goat for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, רבי אליעזר agrees he does not bring an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי אליעזר agrees that the king does not bring a guilt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן makes a new statement about רבי אליעזר's view. Even רבי אליעזר agrees that the נשיא does not bring an אשם for טומאת מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12, רבי יוחנן said that רבי אליעזר treats the נשיא's sin of טומאת מקדש like a fixed sin-offering, so the נשיא brings a goat. Now רבי יוחנן puts a limit on that comparison. It does not stretch so far that the נשיא would also bring an אשם, the guilt-offering brought when someone is unsure whether he sinned.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees; concedes a point even within his own view
Guilt-offering; here it means the אשם תלוי brought when one is unsure whether he sinned

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Rabbi Eliezer agrees
that he does not bring a guilt-offering.
phrases.notes: "He" is the נשיא, and the case is still טומאת מקדש וקדשיו from step 12.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to רבי אליעזר's view as רבי יוחנן explained it in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to רבי אליעזר, the נשיא does not bring an אשם (תלוי) for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a provisional guilt-offering is brought for defiling the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רב ששת: an אשם תלוי is brought for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reciter taught before רב ששת: a provisional guilt-offering comes for defiling the מקדש and its holy foods.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא is quoted saying that an אשם תלוי is brought for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. The גמרא is setting this up so רב ששת can react to it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually, an אשם תלוי is brought only for sins that would need a fixed sin-offering if the person knew for sure he had sinned. טומאת מקדש normally gets a sliding-scale offering, so this ברייתא is surprising. It needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: A reciter in the study hall who memorized and repeated משניות and ברייתות
Provisional ("hanging") guilt-offering, brought when one is unsure whether he sinned
Entering the מקדש or eating holy food while impure

phrases.english: The reciter taught before Rav Sheshet:
A provisional guilt-offering comes
for defiling the Mikdash and its holy foods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that seems to clash with what רבי יוחנן just said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם תלוי is brought for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

steps.title: רב ששת says the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says this ברייתא must follow רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר treats טומאת מקדש like a fixed-offering sin, so the נשיא brings a goat for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Who told you this? It is רבי אליעזר, who said: since כרת is stated about it just as with a fixed sin-offering, the king brings a goat for it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת works out whose view the ברייתא follows. He says it is רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that since טומאת מקדש carries כרת like the sins that need a fixed sin-offering, the נשיא brings a goat. רב ששת's logic is that if it counts as a fixed-offering sin, then when there is doubt, an אשם תלוי should also apply. That would explain the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Who? Used to ask which תנא a teaching follows
Spiritual cutting-off, the punishment for certain deliberate sins
A fixed sin-offering, meaning one set animal, not a sliding-scale offering
Male goat, the נשיא's sin-offering

phrases.english: He said to him: Who is it that told you this?
phrases.notes: רב ששת is asking which תנא this ברייתא follows, and he answers his own question right away.

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Eliezer, who said:
since כרת is stated about it as with a fixed sin-offering,
the king brings a goat for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּאֲמַר לָךְ מַנִּי? רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies which תנא the ברייתא from step 17 follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא that requires an אשם תלוי for טומאת מקדש follows רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: But רבי יוחנן said רבי אליעזר agrees there is no provisional guilt-offering
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת's explanation clashes with רבי יוחנן's statement that even רבי אליעזר agrees the נשיא brings no אשם תלוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יוחנן say: רבי אליעזר agrees that he does not bring a provisional guilt-offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא was just tied to רבי אליעזר, so the גמרא raises a problem. רבי יוחנן said that רבי אליעזר himself agrees there is no אשם תלוי here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the ברייתא has no one who could hold it. רבי אליעזר is ruled out by רבי יוחנן's statement in step 16. The רבנן who disagree with him certainly don't treat טומאת מקדש as a fixed-offering sin.

keyTerms.meaning: "But didn't [so-and-so] say...!", a formula for raising a contradiction

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
Rabbi Eliezer agrees
that he does not bring a provisional guilt-offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's claim that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר (step 18).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן said that even רבי אליעזר holds there is no אשם תלוי here, so the ברייתא cannot be following him.

steps.title: The question is left unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with the word קשיא: the ברייתא stays a difficulty against רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits it has no answer. The contradiction between the ברייתא and רבי יוחנן stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain "קשיא" means the problem is real and unsolved. It does not mean either side is completely thrown out. The discussion of the נשיא and טומאת מקדש ends here.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is difficult": the question stands without an answer

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, even רבי אליעזר holds the נשיא brings no אשם תלוי for טומאת מקדש. The ברייתא that says otherwise is left as an unanswered difficulty.
steps.confusionAlert: A final "קשיא" is not the same as "תיובתא" (a full refutation). It only means the question was never answered.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from step 19 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא stays difficult against רבי יוחנן's statement; no answer is given.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק הוריה כהן משיח
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the second פרק of הוריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, "An anointed כהן ruled."
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "הדרן עלך" is a promise to come back and learn this פרק again. The words after it are the name of the פרק, taken from its first words.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you", said when finishing a פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you,
"An anointed כהן ruled"
phrases.notes: This is the name of the פרק that just ended.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the פרק after the final קשיא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second פרק of הוריות is complete.

steps.title: A כהן משיח or נשיא who leaves office: before or after the sin
steps.stepSummary: If he sinned and then left office, the כהן משיח brings a bull and the נשיא brings a goat. If he left office and then sinned, the כהן משיח still brings a bull, but the נשיא is like an ordinary person.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: An anointed כהן who sinned and afterward left his anointed position, and likewise a נשיא who sinned and afterward left his greatness: the anointed כהן brings a bull, and the נשיא brings a goat. An anointed כהן who left his anointed position and afterward sinned, and likewise a נשיא who left his greatness and afterward sinned: the anointed כהן brings a bull, and the נשיא is like a commoner.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה. It asks what offering a כהן משיח or a נשיא brings if he is no longer in office.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the sin happened while he was still in office, both men bring their special offerings, even after they step down. When the sin happened after they stepped down, the two are treated differently. The כהן משיח still brings a bull, but the former נשיא brings the regular offering of an ordinary person.

keyTerms.meaning: The anointed כהן גדול
His anointed position as כהן גדול
His greatness, meaning the נשיא's position of rule
Bull, the כהן משיח's sin-offering
A commoner, an ordinary person

steps.whyThisMatters: The משנה shows a difference between the two roles. The כהן משיח keeps his special offering even when he sins after leaving office, but the נשיא does not.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the order in each case. "Sinned then left" and "left then sinned" give different results for the נשיא but the same result for the כהן משיח.

phrases.english: MISHNAH: An anointed כהן who sinned
and afterward left his anointed position,
and likewise a נשיא who sinned
and afterward left his greatness:
the anointed כהן brings a bull,
and the נשיא brings a goat.
An anointed כהן who left his anointed position
and afterward sinned,
and likewise the נשיא who left his greatness
and afterward sinned:
the anointed כהן brings a bull,
and the נשיא is like a commoner.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ כֹּהֵן מָשִׁיחַ שֶׁחָטָא וְאַחַר כָּךְ עָבַר מִמְּשִׁיחוּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the Hadran.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sinned then left office: a bull for the כהן משיח and a goat for the נשיא. Left office then sinned: a bull for the כהן משיח, and the נשיא brings what an ordinary person brings.

steps.title: The גמרא starts questioning the wording of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with "Now it can be said: he left his anointed position...", the start of a question about how the משנה is arranged.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Now it can be said: he left his anointed position,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a question about the משנה's wording. This line is only the setup, and the question is finished in the lines that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "השתא" ("now that...") usually starts a "now that we know X, isn't Y obvious?" kind of argument. Here the גמרא points to the case where he left office first. That suggests it will ask why the משנה needed to teach the other case.

keyTerms.meaning: "Now": opens a "now that this is so, then surely..." argument
"It can be said": introduces what we could already conclude

phrases.english: GEMARA: Now it can be said:
he left his anointed position,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's discussion of the new משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way the משנה lists its cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The "השתא" opening sets up an argument that one case should already be obvious from the other; the full challenge continues in the next lines.
